summary: Read a sequence of tokens. Each token is either an integer or one of add, subtract, multiply, and divide. Tokens are written in reverse Polish order. When an operator appears, it acts on the two results sitting just before it, and the earlier result is the left operand. Division truncates toward zero and keeps only the integer quotient. The expression can always be finished and never uses zero as a divisor. Write the final integer.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is a count followed by that many strings.
